import pandas as pd

# Load the datasets
df_offshoring = pd.read_stata('/data/offshoring_iv_mar2.dta')
df_immi = pd.read_stata('/data/immi_popimputed_00_07.dta')

# Display the first few rows of each dataset
df_offshoring.head(), df_immi.head()

# Merge the datasets on 'year' and 'beaind'
df_merged = pd.merge(df_offshoring, df_immi, on=['year', 'beaind'], how='inner')

# Display the first few rows of the merged dataset
df_merged.head()

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np

# Prepare the data for regression
X = df_merged[['iv_offshoring_1']].values.reshape(-1, 1)  # Predictor
y = df_merged['share_immi_imputed'].values  # Response

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficient and p-value
coefficient = model.coef_[0]
p_value = model.score(X, y)

coefficient, p_value

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Check the distribution of the variables
sns.histplot(df_merged['iv_offshoring_1'], kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of iv_offshoring_1')
plt.show()

sns.histplot(df_merged['share_immi_imputed'], kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of share_immi_imputed')
plt.show()

# Check for multicollinearity
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor

vif_data = pd.DataFrame()
vif_data["feature"] = df_merged[['iv_offshoring_1', 'share_immi_imputed']].columns
vif_data["VIF"] = [variance_inflation_factor(df_merged[['iv_offshoring_1', 'share_immi_imputed']].values, i) for i in range(df_merged[['iv_offshoring_1', 'share_immi_imputed']].shape[1])]
